fields.title: Free Nurse Resume Checker: score your RN resume against the job posting
fields.h1: A resume checker that knows what a nursing resume needs
fields.lede: Paste your resume and the posting. It scores both, shows the exact line behind every finding, and rewrites the weak bullets. No signup, and your resume never leaves your browser.
fields.who: RNs, LPNs, CNAs, nurse practitioners, techs and clinical staff
numbers: patients per shift, and the acuity level
bed count on your unit
medication error rate, or time with zero errors
fall rate, readmission rate, or infection rate you moved
nurses you precepted, and how many passed on the first attempt
response times on rapid response or code events
fields.trap: Most nursing resumes list duties every nurse shares. "Provided patient care" tells a manager nothing, because it is true of everyone applying. The fix is scope and outcome: how many patients, how sick, and what changed.

fields.title: Free Electrician Resume Checker: score your trade resume against the job
fields.h1: A resume checker built for the trades, not for software jobs
fields.lede: Most resume tools were written for office work. This one knows what a journeyman card is worth and what counts as proof on a job site. Free, no signup, nothing uploaded.
fields.who: Electricians, welders, HVAC techs, plumbers, millwrights, mechanics and maintenance crews
numbers: downtime you cut, in hours or percent
feet of conduit, cable tray or pipe run
voltage and system size you worked on
incident free hours or days on site
square footage of the facility
units, machines or panels you maintained
fields.trap: Trade resumes get judged on the same rules as everyone else, which is unfair but real. The winning move is numbers, because your work produces them naturally. Downtime, footage, voltage, incident free hours. Most people leave all of it off.

fields.title: Free Teacher Resume Checker: score your teaching resume against the posting
fields.h1: A resume checker that understands a teaching resume
fields.lede: It looks for the things a principal and a district screening system actually check, and shows you the line behind every point. Free, no account, nothing leaves your browser.
fields.who: Classroom teachers, paraeducators, counselors, instructional coaches and school staff
numbers: class size and number of sections
growth on a assessment, in points or percent
pass rates or proficiency rates you moved
students served across a year
attendance or behavior referrals you reduced
colleagues you mentored or trained
fields.trap: Teaching resumes drift into philosophy. Districts screen for evidence. One line with growth data beats a paragraph about your approach to learning, because the first can be checked and the second cannot.

fields.title: Free CDL Driver and Warehouse Resume Checker
fields.h1: A resume checker for drivers, warehouse and operations work
fields.lede: Scores your resume against the job posting and shows what to fix, in plain language. Free, no signup, and nothing is uploaded anywhere.
fields.who: CDL drivers, warehouse leads, forklift operators, dispatchers, supervisors and logistics staff
numbers: safe miles driven, and years without an accident
loads or stops per day
on time delivery rate
units picked or shipped per shift
headcount you supervised
cost per unit or per mile you cut
creds: endorsements such as hazmat or tanker
fields.trap: Driving and warehouse resumes often list equipment and leave out performance. Safety record and on time rate are the two numbers that get you called, and almost nobody puts them on the page.

fields.title: Free Accountant and Finance Resume Checker
fields.h1: A resume checker for accounting and finance roles
fields.lede: It checks the things a finance hiring manager screens for and shows the exact line behind every finding. Free, no account needed, nothing uploaded.
fields.who: Accountants, bookkeepers, analysts, auditors, AP and AR staff and finance managers
numbers: portfolio or budget size you handled
days to close, and how much you cut it
variance identified or recovered, in dollars
accounts or transactions per month
audit findings closed
cost savings you delivered
fields.trap: Finance resumes say "responsible for month end close" instead of "cut close from twelve days to seven". The second one is the same job described in a way that can be checked.

fields.title: Free Resume Checker, No Signup and No Upload
fields.h1: A free resume checker that does not ask you to sign up
fields.lede: No account, no email, no card, and no free trial that turns into a charge. Paste your resume and a job posting and get the full result, including the fixes.
fields.who: Anyone applying for a job, in any field
numbers: money saved or earned
time cut from a process
people trained, managed or served
volume handled per day, week or month
error or defect rate you reduced
percentage improvement, with the starting point
fields.trap: Most free resume checkers show you a score and put the fixes behind a signup. This one shows you everything, because the fixes are the only part that helps and the score on its own is useless.

fields.title: Free ATS Resume Checker: see what a resume scanner reads
fields.h1: An ATS resume checker that shows its rubric
fields.lede: It checks the things applicant tracking systems are known to check, and publishes the whole scoring rubric so you can see where every point went. Free and nothing is uploaded.
fields.who: Anyone whose resume keeps disappearing into online applications
numbers: any figure that proves the result rather than describing the task
percentages, with the starting number so it can be judged
counts of people, dollars, units or hours
time periods, so the reader knows the pace
creds: Whatever the posting names, in the same words it uses
fields.trap: No tool can tell you exactly what Workday or Taleo scored you, because none of them publish it. Be careful with any product that claims a real ATS score. What can be checked is whether your file parses, whether the posting's words appear, and whether your claims carry evidence.

fields.title: Free Veteran Resume Checker: translate service into civilian terms
fields.h1: A resume checker for veterans moving into civilian work
fields.lede: Scores your resume against a specific posting and shows which military terms are not landing. Free, no account, and nothing about you is uploaded anywhere.
fields.who: Transitioning service members, veterans and military spouses
numbers: people you led, and their rank or level
budget or equipment value you were accountable for
operations, missions or inspections completed
readiness or qualification rates you raised
training hours delivered
incidents avoided or safety record
fields.trap: The usual advice is to strip out all military language. That goes too far. The posting's words matter, so keep what maps cleanly and translate the rest. "Accountable for $4M of equipment with zero losses" needs no translation at all.
